outline.chapter_title: Fundamentals of Tabular Few‑Shot Learning and Large Language Models
outline.description: Introduces the unique characteristics of tabular data, the challenges posed by limited labeled examples, basic inductive biases used by traditional models, and an overview of large language models that enable knowledge transfer through prompting.
subtopics: Structure of tabular datasets – numeric versus categorical columns and natural language feature names
Why few‑shot learning is difficult for tabular problems compared with vision or text domains
Typical inductive biases in decision trees, linear models and gradient boosting
Definition of k‑shot learning setups used throughout the book
Core capabilities of modern large language models that make them useful as knowledge sources
Principle of in‑context learning without updating model parameters

outline.chapter_title: Survey of Prior Approaches to Low‑Shot Tabular Learning
outline.description: Reviews classical baselines as well as recent techniques that incorporate self‑supervision, transfer across tables or language models; highlights their strengths and practical drawbacks that motivate a new direction.
subtopics: Conventional baselines – logistic regression, gradient boosting machines and random forests
(a) Transfer learning across many tables – approaches such as TransTab
(b) Synthetic data pretraining – methods exemplified by TabPFN
(c) Semi‑supervised strategies that leverage unlabeled records – SCARF and STUNT
(d) Language interfaced tabular learning – direct prompting (in‑context), parameter‑efficient tuning (LoRA/IA³), hybrid systems like TABLET
Key limitations encountered by existing methods: per‑sample API calls to an LLM at inference time, need for fine­tuning access or large context windows
